panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Baseline clinical photograph of the axilla in a genetically confirmed Hailey-Hailey disease patient showing an active erosive, macerated intertriginous plaque with a dark crusted surface. The manifestation (flexural erosion with maceration) is a textbook Hailey-Hailey presentation, and the article title and caption confirm disease attribution. No age or ethnicity stated in caption or in-text. B: Baseline clinical photograph of the inguinal/genital intertriginous region in the same genetically confirmed Hailey-Hailey disease patient, showing severe erythema, maceration, superficial erosions, and fissuring. Flexural eroded and fissured plaques are a classic presentation of Hailey-Hailey disease, and attribution is supported by the disease-focused article title and panel-specific caption. No age or ethnicity stated in caption or in-text.

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E histopathology (×200) of a human 4-mm skin punch biopsy from an article on Hailey-Hailey disease. The caption and in-text describe widespread acantholysis at multiple epithelial levels with a 'dilapidated brick wall' appearance, the recognized histological hallmark of HHD, which is clearly visible in the image. Disease attribution is specific and supported by both caption and article title.
panels.attribution_text: Mehrabian et al. The Use of Naltrexone to Successfully Treat Severe Hailey-Hailey Disease.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.110281. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological image with H&E staining, original magnification ×200.
in_text_mentions: A 4-mm punch biopsy was performed. Histology showed hyperkeratosis, patchy parakeratosis, prominent epidermal acanthosis, and widespread acantholysis involving multiple levels of the squamous epithelium, producing a “dilapidated brick wall” appearance. Occasional dyskeratotic cells were also noted. The overall clinicopathological findings were consistent with HHD (Figures 1-2). in_text_mentions: Cutaneous examination revealed multiple hyperpigmented to erythematous plaques predominantly involving intertriginous and flexural areas, including the nape of the neck (Figure 1), bilateral axillae, groin, lower abdominal folds (Figure 2), and flexural aspects of the limbs (Figure 3). The lesions were variably well‐ to ill‐defined, with surface scaling, crusting, and areas of superficial erosion. Areas of maceration and excoriation were noted, suggestive of chronicity with repeated frictional aggravation.

In addition, lesions over the bilateral groins, lower abdominal folds, and flexural aspects of the limbs demonstrated multiple pinpoint to 2–3 mm hyperpigmented macules and papules coalescing into plaques, some with keratotic changes and reticulate to patchy pigmentation (Figures 2 and 3). These areas exhibited a predominantly papular and follicular morphology with prominent post‐inflammatory hyperpigmentation, in contrast to the more erosive and crusted plaques over the neck and axillae.

in_text_mentions: Cutaneous examination revealed multiple hyperpigmented to erythematous plaques predominantly involving intertriginous and flexural areas, including the nape of the neck (Figure 1), bilateral axillae, groin, lower abdominal folds (Figure 2), and flexural aspects of the limbs (Figure 3). The lesions were variably well‐ to ill‐defined, with surface scaling, crusting, and areas of superficial erosion. Areas of maceration and excoriation were noted, suggestive of chronicity with repeated frictional aggravation.

In addition, lesions over the bilateral groins, lower abdominal folds, and flexural aspects of the limbs demonstrated multiple pinpoint to 2–3 mm hyperpigmented macules and papules coalescing into plaques, some with keratotic changes and reticulate to patchy pigmentation (Figures 2 and 3). These areas exhibited a predominantly papular and follicular morphology with prominent post‐inflammatory hyperpigmentation, in contrast to the more erosive and crusted plaques over the neck and axillae.
